scripts/brief.py:49-57 - no cortex_client, ManifestMinter or canonical_manifest_bytes import, so no /v1/contract/submit and no ledger append
G7.reasoning: The figures shown were not executed by Cortex on this path. They are passed through from an unauthenticated JSON, plus one locally derived remainder. Nothing is signed or ledgered, and nothing is checked against a ledger entry.
G7.bypass_scenario: Any report JSON that passes validate_report, real or hand-made, yields a deck whose figures have no Cortex submit, manifest signature or ledger entry. For a long table, the 'the other N groups ... sum to X' line is computed by brief.py itself at :137 and appears on the slide as a figure.

evidence: scripts/brief.py:426-431 - an unreadable or invalid JSON file prints 'FAIL report: cannot read ...' and exits 1
scripts/brief.py:432-436 - validate_report problems print 'FAIL <insight id>: <what is wrong>' and exit 1
scripts/brief.py:441-448 - a slide-count mismatch or a stray deck figure prints FAIL and exits 1
scripts/brief.py:453-455 - an HTML-only run prints 'wrote HTML; no deck built' and never PASS
scripts/brief.py:350 vs :444-448 - build_pptx saves the deck before the read-back, and a failing deck is not removed
scripts/brief.py:297,349-350,450-451 - a missing python-pptx (dev extra only, pyproject.toml:46-57), mkdir/save errors and the HTML write_text are not caught, so they surface as raw tracebacks
G8.reasoning: The data-driven failure branches are named FAIL lines with a non-zero exit, and none produces a confident PASS. Gaps: the docstring promises 'never a traceback' (brief.py:36-38), but environment and IO failures are uncaught. A deck that failed the read-back stays on disk at the output path, with no marker inside it. There is also no named refusal for a report whose own broken list is non-empty, because validate_report never reads it.
G8.bypass_scenario: Run brief.py --insights r.json --pptx out.pptx where r.json is a valid report but a figure on a slide trips the read-back at :445. The run prints FAIL and exits 1, but out.pptx has already been written at :350 and stays on disk. Anyone who ignores the exit code, such as a script or someone who just opens the file, gets a deck with an unaccounted figure and no FAIL marker inside it.

other_findings: scripts/brief.py:163-166 and :182-263 - the provenance claim 'Every figure compiled and conserved.' is unconditional. validate_report never reads report['broken'] or insight['conserves'] (grep for broken/conserves in brief.py finds only the docstring word 'unbroken' at :9). scripts/insights.py:430 writes the JSON before its failure exit (:432-439), so a failing insights run, or a hand-edited report, still yields a deck carrying that claim.
scripts/brief.py:385-398 - deck_numbers scans slide.shapes text frames and tables only. The speaker notes holding the SQL (:334) are not read back, so numbers in the notes are not checked.
scripts/brief.py:401-405 - verify_deck compares sets of numeric tokens, so it cannot catch figures swapped between rows or between slides, only a token the report lacks.
scripts/brief.py:297 - python-pptx is a dev-only extra (pyproject.toml:46-57), so --pptx in a non-dev install fails with ModuleNotFoundError instead of a named FAIL.
